parts.name: base body

physics.Basic_description: The main black base of the stapler, appearing as a matte plastic rectangular prism with rounded edges.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural foundation and stability for the stapler on a desk surface.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can grasp the sides or top surface of the base to hold the stapler steady during operation.
physics.reason: Injection molded plastic housing typically encloses empty space or ribs to save material and weight.

parts.description: The main black base of the stapler, appearing as a matte plastic rectangular prism with rounded edges.
parts.function: Provides the structural foundation and stability for the stapler on a desk surface.

parts.name: base feet

physics.Basic_description: Small dark pads located on the underside of the base, likely rubber or soft plastic.
physics.Functional_description: Prevents the stapler from sliding on smooth surfaces and protects the desk from scratches.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flat against the surface to be a primary grasp target.
physics.reason: Small anti-slip pads are typically solid pieces of rubber or foam adhered to the base.

parts.description: Small dark pads located on the underside of the base, likely rubber or soft plastic.
parts.function: Prevents the stapler from sliding on smooth surfaces and protects the desk from scratches.

parts.name: anvil plate

physics.Basic_description: A silver metallic plate embedded in the rear of the black base.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a hard surface with grooves to bend the staple legs inward or outward after piercing paper.
physics.Grasped_description: Flush with the base and too small to grasp independently.
physics.reason: Must be a solid metal piece to withstand the impact force of stapling without deforming.

parts.description: A silver metallic plate embedded in the rear of the black base.
parts.function: Provides a hard surface with grooves to bend the staple legs inward or outward after piercing paper.

parts.name: hinge knuckles

physics.Basic_description: Yellowish-metallic cylindrical components at the rear connecting the top arm to the base.
physics.Functional_description: Forms the pivot point allowing the top arm to rotate open and closed.
physics.Grasped_description: Small and located at the joint, not suitable for grasping.
physics.reason: Hinge components must be solid to support the mechanical load of the stapling action.

parts.description: Yellowish-metallic cylindrical components at the rear connecting the top arm to the base.
parts.function: Forms the pivot point allowing the top arm to rotate open and closed.

parts.name: arm shell

physics.Basic_description: The large blue upper handle of the stapler, with a smooth matte plastic finish.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the lever arm; user presses down on this to drive staples through paper.
physics.Grasped_description: The primary interaction point; a gripper would grasp the top or sides of this shell to operate the stapler.
physics.reason: This is a cosmetic cover shell over the internal metal mechanism, definitely hollow to reduce weight and cost.

parts.description: The large blue upper handle of the stapler, with a smooth matte plastic finish.
parts.function: Acts as the lever arm; user presses down on this to drive staples through paper.

parts.name: carrier rail

physics.Basic_description: A purple-colored strip visible inside the top arm in the segmentation, representing the internal metal channel.
physics.Functional_description: Guides the strip of staples and provides the track for the driver mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal component, generally not accessible for grasping without disassembly.
physics.reason: Staple channels are typically formed from bent sheet metal, creating a U-shaped profile with air inside.

parts.description: A purple-colored strip visible inside the top arm in the segmentation, representing the internal metal channel.
parts.function: Guides the strip of staples and provides the track for the driver mechanism.

parts.name: driver blade

physics.Basic_description: A small cyan-colored metal tip at the front of the top arm.
physics.Functional_description: The blade that physically pushes the staple out of the magazine and through the paper.
physics.Grasped_description: Tiny functional tip, not a grasp target.
physics.reason: Must be a solid, hardened metal piece to transfer force without buckling.

parts.description: A small cyan-colored metal tip at the front of the top arm.
parts.function: The blade that physically pushes the staple out of the magazine and through the paper.

parts.name: hinge pin

physics.Basic_description: A small magenta-colored pin located at the hinge assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Secures the top arm to the base knuckles, acting as the axle for rotation.
physics.reason: Pins are solid cylinders of metal designed to resist shear forces.

parts.description: A small magenta-colored pin located at the hinge assembly.
parts.function: Secures the top arm to the base knuckles, acting as the axle for rotation.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
